text:
jordan: Quick benefits question — I'm leaving Redwood on 2026-07-02 and want to rollover my 401(k) to an IRA. Two parts: can I do a direct rollover after termination (how long do I have)? And separately, can I convert that balance to a Roth during rollover or does that trigger withholding/penalties? Also, will any outstanding pre-tax HSA payroll contributions need to be reconciled on final pay?

elaine: You can usually do a direct trustee-to-trustee rollover after termination. PlanHive allows direct rollovers; you should request it within 60 days to avoid taxable distribution reporting, but direct rollover avoids the 60-day rule.

ben: For timing: final payroll is 2026-07-01 (runs the day before termination date). If there are salary deferrals or HSA contributions pending, they need coding before that cutoff. HSA contributions deducted from payroll will stop after your last payroll; any employer contributions are prorated.

jordan: If I do an indirect rollover (they send me a check), what's withheld? And can I convert to Roth as part of the rollover process?

toni: Indirect rollover: 20% mandatory federal tax withheld on distributions. You'd need to replace the withheld amount from other funds within 60 days to avoid tax/penalty on the part not rolled. Converting to Roth is allowed, but if you convert pre-tax funds to Roth, that amount is taxable in the year of conversion. No early withdrawal penalty if it's a rollover+conversion, but you pay income tax. Recommend direct rollover to an IRA then do a Roth conversion at the IRA custodian to control withholding.

planbot: PlanHive policy note: "Distributions on termination are subject to plan terms. Direct trustee-to-trustee rollovers are permitted. If a distribution is made payable to the participant, mandatory 20% federal withholding applies for eligible rollover distributions. Participant has 60 days to complete rollover to avoid taxation. Roth conversions processed by custodian are taxable events."

elaine: Action items: Jordan, submit a distribution form to PlanHive (choose direct rollover) before 2026-07-15. If you prefer direct transfer to Fidelity (or another custodian), include the receiving account info and Fed tax ID. If you want payroll to try to capture any last-minute HSA deferrals, confirm with payroll by 2026-06-29 EOD.

ben: Note on ability to convert during vendor migration: we have a payroll vendor migration 2026-06-10-06-14 but that only affects payroll flows. Rollover requests handled by PlanHive are separate. If you plan ACH repayment or any adjustments, coordinate both teams.

jordan: Cool, thanks. One more: I have a small outstanding loan on the 401(k) (~$1,100). If I do a direct rollover, can I also roll the loan?

toni: Loans generally cannot be rolled over. Outstanding loan balance may be treated as a taxable distribution unless repaid prior to termination or within the plan's cure period. Check PlanHive loan policy.

planbot: Loan record: LoanID 552334, balance $1,100, orig date 2025-03-02. PlanHive loan policy: "Loans cannot be rolled over. Outstanding loans at termination that are not repaid within the plan's cure period are reported as distributions."

elaine: Practical options: repay loan before last payroll (payroll withholding) or pay PlanHive via ACH/wire. If unpaid, rollover amount will be net of distribution (and taxed).

jordan: Okay I'm going to request direct rollover. Thanks everyone. I'll post the PlanHive form once submitted.

ben: FYI — send payroll any HSA questions to payroll@redwood by EOD 2026-06-29. They can confirm year-to-date deferral numbers for your new custodian.

elaine: tagging legal if unusual tax questions: @toni already chimed in. All good. :thumbsup:
